items.title: 48 HOURS. ZERO >10m GAPS. HackMe 0.1.0-rc13 is live.
items.summary: The pool held a continuous 48-hour soak: 0 snapshot gaps over 10 minutes, ~69–197 GH/s (avg ~137), 8–20 workers online (avg ~13), and tip ~199444 → ~203990. Hub 0.1.0-rc12w mining stayed up; after coordinator restarts, the fleet recovered.
items.impact: This is evidence for operator/private-pool readiness: useful-PoW mining, hybrid dig/fuzz work, and HMC/SUP ledger settlement stayed observable under a real fleet. It is not a claim of a trustless L1, exchange readiness, or CEX readiness.

items.summary: Customer bootstrap path held through the night: overnight cjson Audit finished 2000/2000 with escrow closed clean; jsmn recovered from a frozen ~1421 settle tip to full catch-up (~22.6k runs paid). items.title: B2B audits that CI can trust — crash-first reports · honest Scan/Audit/Deep
items.summary: Customer path is productized: register → wizard (Scan · Audit · Deep) → status → HTML report + CI gate. Crash-first triage means detector noise never fails the gate. Escrow 20/80 stays transparent; PoH miners auto-switch to orders while workerfuzz fleets dig pool fuzz. Example: HackMe Bootstrap Audit · cjson — runs progressing, gate crash-first, clean / no critical crash-class.
items.impact: Protocol and security teams get a deliverable they can wire into pipelines — PASS/FAIL on crash-class findings only, plus an honest assurance note (not proven secure). No fake CVE theater: CLEAN means no crash/hang/ASan/memory at the budgeted runs.
